subject: EU-WEST ingress backpressure causing cascading 5xx during Clearline settlement window
messages:
From: Katie Morris <katie.morris@clearline.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Clearline SRE <sre@clearline.com>
Date: 2028-05-25T08:14:22Z
Subject: Spike of 502/503 during nightly settlement window - immediate help needed

Hi Rishi,

We saw a sharp increase in 502/503 responses from the EU-WEST region between 02:15-02:45 UTC during last night's settlement batch. Error rate peaked ~28% for ~18 minutes, downstream timeouts at Clearline's side and payment settlements failed for ~4k requests. We captured a few request/response samples and metrics in the attached clearline_error_samples.log and a screenshot of the LB metrics (eu-ingress-metrics-20280525.png).

This is impacting our reconciliation cutoff; our ops team is asking for a mitigation plan before tonight's window. Can Redwood do any immediate routing/throttling changes, or temporarily route Clearline traffic to another region while you investigate?

Also, please advise if this qualifies for SLA credits — we will need an official statement for our procurement group.

Thanks,
Katie Morris
Head of Payments Ops
Clearline Finance

PS — we can join a quick bridge if helpful, I'm available now or at 13:00 UTC.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Katie Morris <katie.morris@clearline.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-25T08:29:10Z
Subject: Re: Spike of 502/503 during nightly settlement window - immediate help needed

Katie — thanks for the samples and the heads up. We're treating this as a high-severity incident.

Initial triage notes (10:29 UTC):
- Ingress LB in eu-west shows a sudden 3x increase in connection resets and 502/503s aligned with Clearline's traffic pattern (02:12-02:48 UTC).
- There is a short-lived surge in concurrent KV cache lookups for model-context keys used by your flows; we see elevated backend latency and queueing.
- No recent config rollouts to your tenant in the last 72 hours.

Immediate actions we propose (can execute now if you approve):
1) Temporarily divert 30% of Clearline traffic away from the primary eu-west LB to eu-central to reduce contention (will add ~20–40ms RTT).
2) Apply a conservative circuit-breaker on long-tail requests for 60 minutes (drop inflight requests that exceed 15s).
3) Enable additional worker processes on eu-west gateway pool and bump backend concurrency for Clearline route.
4) Collect full proxy traces and full request/response logs for the 02:12-02:48 window (we will share a scrubbed bundle).

I'll create a Jira (INF-9843) and loop our SREs. Can you confirm we should proceed with (1) and (2) immediately? Also please confirm a time window for tonight's settlement (your ETA for when the batch runs) so we can target mitigation in advance.

I can join a call at 13:00 UTC.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-25T09:02:03Z
Subject: Re: Spike of 502/503 during nightly settlement window - immediate help needed

Quick SRE note:
- Symptoms look like ingress queue amplification coupled with upstream slowdowns in a subset of backends that handle cached context (small set of hot keys). When that path slows, connection queues grow at the LB and start to generate timeouts/502/503.
- Created INF-9843 and attached an initial heap of logs and the metric snapshot.

Short-term mitigation I can enact now (60 min TTL):
- Increase backend pool size for your tenant's route by 30% in eu-west.
- Apply a token-bucket rate limit on overly-bursty IPs from Clearline that exceed settlement window baselines.
- Enable per-route KV cache warming and increase cache TTL for the hot keys to reduce backend lookups.

These changes are low-risk and reversible; Marcus will coordinate the rollout and monitor.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE Manager, Serving Runtime
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-25T10:17:45Z
Subject: INTERNAL: Clearline EU ingress P1 — exec update draft

Team — drafting an exec-facing summary to send to the Clearline exec sponsors after we stabilize. Draft below (please review/edit):

Summary (for execs):
- Incident: Elevated 5xx/502/503 error rate in eu-west during Clearline's nightly settlement window (02:12–02:48 UTC).
- Impact: ~4k failed settlement requests, peak error rate ~28%, customer-facing reconciliation impacts during the window.
- Immediate mitigations: traffic diversion to eu-central (30%), temporary circuit-breaker on long-tail requests, backend pool scale-up, per-route throttling.
- Next steps: full postmortem, targeted runtime fix for KV hotspotting, and an offer for a credit per SLA while we complete RCA.

Please add any data points or changes. Once we have stabilization confirmation from Marcus, I will send this to Katie and cc our account exec (Sean).

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
VP, Customer Success

From: Katie Morris <katie.morris@clearline.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Porter <ops@clearline-fin.com>, Clearline SRE <sre@clearline.com>
Date: 2028-05-25T11:03:20Z
Subject: Re: Spike of 502/503 during nightly settlement window - immediate help needed

Rishi / team — thanks for the fast response. Please proceed with the traffic diversion (30%) and the circuit-breaker for the next 60 minutes. We will also accept backend pool scaling.

For tonight's settlement: the next batch runs at 02:20 UTC (approx), and we have a buffer period from 02:00–03:00. If you can have mitigations in place by 02:00 UTC that would be ideal.

On SLA credits: our procurement will need an initial statement and the incident ticket number to start the credit request — INF-9843 should be fine.

I can join a post-mortem call tomorrow after your RCA is available.

Thanks,
Katie

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Katie Morris <katie.morris@clearline.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-25T16:42:05Z
Subject: Resolution: temporary mitigations applied and next steps (Clearline EU ingress incident)

Katie — quick update following today's actions and monitoring: we applied the diversion of ~30% traffic to eu-central at 01:45 UTC, enabled the 15s circuit-breaker at 01:48 UTC, and increased the eu-west backend pool by 35% at 01:50 UTC.

Result: the 502/503 rate dropped from 28% peak to <1.5% within 7 minutes of the mitigations. We continued monitoring through the 02:20 UTC settlement window without further failures.

Next steps and ownership:
- INF-9843 (Marcus) — RCA to identify KV cache hotspotting and a remediation plan for runtime-level fixes (owner: Marcus Lin).
- Postmortem (Evelyn) — schedule for 48 hours; include SLA credit language and customer-facing summary (owner: Evelyn Hart).
- Long-term (Olga) — consider LB-level admission control and adaptive routing to prevent similar amplification across tenants (owner: Olga Petrov).

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_clearline_v1.xlsx (proposed runbook + rollback plan), scrubbed logs bundle (clearline_error_samples.log), metric snapshot (eu-ingress-metrics-20280525.png).

I'll send the exec summary to your sponsors after Evelyn's review and include the official incident ticket. Thank you and sorry for the disruption — we'll follow up with the postmortem and a formal SLA statement.

—Rishi
